content:
Jonas Weber: circling back on the gating-mode stats. we need to lock: (1) min sample size per suite (2) what we do about flaky rubric graders (3) rerun policy. current drafts are hand-wavy.

Selene Huang: +1. we’re already seeing borderline fails in pilot where the deltas are within noise. if we don’t define “inconclusive” and rerun rules, we’ll end up either blocking too much or letting stuff slip.

Sana Farid: ok, let’s pin what “min sample size” is trying to guarantee. if we use CI-based gating (non-inferiority), the CI width depends on N + variance. so a fixed N across all suites is kinda wrong.

Karthik Iyer: agree. but we also can’t do adaptive sampling that takes 30 minutes for some suites. optimize apply needs bounded runtime.

Olivia Grant: remind me of the operational constraint: apply flow wants <10 min p95 for gating results (with async job)?

Jonas Weber: yep. for pilot we’re targeting ~5 min median, 10 min p95. and we also want to avoid rerunning 3x and blowing up queues.

Sana Farid: proposal: define per-suite “target N” + “hard min N” and then CI rule. e.g.
- smoke/sentinel: hard min 30, target 50
- core task suite: hard min 100, target 200
- long-context/formatting suite: hard min 60, target 120
if suite has fewer than hard min prompts, gating returns INCONCLUSIVE.

Selene Huang: how do we pick those numbers without making it arbitrary? (someone will ask why 100 vs 120)

Sana Farid: we can justify via historical variance. most rubric metrics have stddev ~0.35 on 0-5 scale across prompts. with N=200, SE ~0.025; 95% CI ~ +/-0.05-ish in score units. that’s usually enough to detect the regressions we care about (>=0.1-0.15 score drop) without false flags.

Karthik Iyer: but rubric scores aren’t normal, and there’s grader variance too.

Sana Farid: yep. for gating we should avoid distributional assumptions and use bootstrap CIs on the paired deltas (candidate - baseline) per prompt.

Jonas Weber: paired bootstrap is what i was leaning toward anyway. we can treat each prompt as a paired sample and compute delta distribution.

Diego Ramos: +1 on paired. also helps with prompt difficulty mix changing.

Selene Huang: ok but the “paired” part depends on running baseline and candidate on the same prompt set revision + same grader. are we doing that?

Olivia Grant: eval-harness gating mode uses prompt-set rev pinned + baseline config snapshot. baseline run is either cached or rerun if missing.

Jonas Weber: baseline caching is in the plan, but in the meantime: yes same prompts. grader model version also needs to be pinned.

Sahana Iyer: pinning grader model version is necessary but not sufficient. we’ve still got nondeterminism (temperature >0, provider drift, tool timeouts).

Sana Farid: exactly. we need “flaky grader” detection. i’d define flakiness as high disagreement across repeated grading of the SAME response.

Karthik Iyer: do we actually have budget to grade twice?

Sana Farid: not everything. but for rubric-based metrics that gate (task_success_rubric, instruction_following_rubric), i think we need at least 2x grading on a subset to estimate grader noise.

Jonas Weber: subset approach seems practical. like: grade all once, and for 10% sample, grade again with different seed. compute repeatability.

Selene Huang: what threshold would trigger a rerun vs just widening CI?

Sana Farid: two things:
1) “grader_error_rate”: % of prompts where rubric output invalid / missing required fields.
2) “grader_repeatability”: avg absolute diff between grade1 and grade2 on the 10% sample.
If error_rate > 2% OR repeatability > 0.35 (on 0-5), mark suite as UNSTABLE and return INCONCLUSIVE (not fail).

Sahana Iyer: 2% might be tight. we’ve seen transient JSON parse failures around 1-3% depending on provider. but if we pin to our own hosted grader model it should be <1%.

Jonas Weber: for pilot, we’re using the internal grader endpoint (redwood-judge-v2). so 2% seems fine.

Karthik Iyer: question: if suite is UNSTABLE, do we rerun automatically or require manual?

Selene Huang: i’d prefer one automatic rerun if the reason is infrastructure-ish (timeouts, judge errors). otherwise people will just hit “rerun” a bunch and we’ll pretend it’s science.

Sana Farid: +1. auto rerun once, but only when failure mode indicates non-quality issue.

Jonas Weber: can we enumerate the rerun conditions precisely?

Sana Farid: draft:
- Auto rerun ONCE if:
  a) judge_error_rate > 2% OR judge_timeouts > 1% OR artifact_upload_failed
  b) suite_total_completed < hard_min due to worker preemption
- Auto rerun ONCE if gating result is “borderline”:
  c) CI overlaps threshold by small margin: e.g., lower_bound within 0.01 of threshold for normalized metrics
But (c) is controversial.

Karthik Iyer: i don’t love (c). that’s where you can rerun until you pass.

Selene Huang: yeah, borderline rerun turns into “rerun lottery”. we should treat borderline as INCONCLUSIVE and require override/approval if they want to apply.

Diego Ramos: +1. also better for auditability: “inconclusive due to insufficient power” is defensible.

Jonas Weber: ok so rerun only for infra / obvious flake, not for borderline quality.

Sana Farid: works. then we need to define when we return FAIL vs INCONCLUSIVE.

Selene Huang: current UX spec has Pass / Fail / Timeout. maybe we need “Inconclusive” as a first-class state (or map it to Fail with a specific reason?).

Olivia Grant: UI already has “partial/timeout” state drafts. adding “inconclusive” is doable but needs copy + legal review (we don’t want to imply we tested and it’s safe).

Jonas Weber: for now we can keep it as Fail with reason_code=INCONCLUSIVE and a friendly message: “Couldn’t make a confident decision; rerun or request override.”

Sana Farid: ok. now, min sample size per suite. i still think hard min is needed. but do we also need per-metric min? some metrics have missingness (tool calling success only applies when tools invoked).

Karthik Iyer: yes. otherwise you can have N=200 prompts but only 12 tool calls and the tool metric is meaningless.

Sana Farid: then rule should be:
- suite_min_prompts: hard min
- metric_min_effective_n: per metric (after filtering to applicable prompts)
If any gated metric has effective_n < metric_min_effective_n => INCONCLUSIVE.

Jonas Weber: numbers?

Sana Farid: suggest metric_min_effective_n defaults:
- binary pass/fail metrics: 60
- rubric avg score: 100
- formatting/JSON validity: 80
- toxicity (rare events): 200 (or treat as “max increase” style constraint)

Selene Huang: toxicity gating in optimize apply is tricky. we shouldn’t block a quantization change because toxicity on 200 prompts bounced by 1 example.

Sana Farid: agree. toxicity should be “no worse than baseline + epsilon” with a bigger epsilon and maybe use a one-sided CI on rate difference.

Karthik Iyer: also multiple metrics = multiple comparisons. if we gate on 8 metrics at alpha=0.05 we will false-fail often.

Sana Farid: yep. simplest: don’t treat these as hypothesis tests. treat them as guardrails with effect-size thresholds + CI non-inferiority, but no strict alpha. then no need for Holm-Bonferroni.

Jonas Weber: so: for each metric, compute delta + bootstrap CI (95%). pass if lower_bound >= -allowed_regression. and only if effective_n >= min.

Selene Huang: what about “strictly better” metrics? e.g., we might allow latency to change but that’s not in quality gating.

Jonas Weber: quality only here.

Sahana Iyer: for flakiness: can we log judge model version + seed + temperature? so we can reproduce.

Olivia Grant: yep. gating output format already includes judge_model, judge_prompt_rev, and we can add judge_params.

Diego Ramos: another thought: for flaky rubric graders, maybe compare baseline vs candidate with the same *responses*, only re-grade? i.e. freeze model outputs and isolate grader noise.

Sana Farid: that’s actually a good debug mode. for gating we can’t do it because responses differ between configs. but for investigating a suspected false fail, “regrade frozen outputs” helps identify grader drift.

Jonas Weber: action item: add triage playbook step: if fail is rubric-based and close to threshold, do regrade-only job to measure judge variance.

Selene Huang: +1, and in UI we should link “rerun (infra)” vs “request override” vs “open investigation”.

Karthik Iyer: ok can we settle on concrete N for pilot? we can iterate but need something now.

Sana Farid: for pilot tiers:
- Core suite (chat + instruct): hard min 120 prompts, target 200
- Tool-calling suite: hard min 80 prompts, plus tool_metric effective_n >= 40
- Structured-output suite: hard min 80 prompts
- Long-context suite: hard min 60 prompts
All computed with paired bootstrap on deltas.

Jonas Weber: i’m good with that.

Selene Huang: same. can we add: if suite runtime exceeds 12 min => TIMEOUT => treat as INCONCLUSIVE (not PASS). no apply.

Olivia Grant: yep. control plane already blocks on timeout unless override feature flag.

Sahana Iyer: re reruns: do we rerun on timeout automatically? careful, that can double load during an outage.

Jonas Weber: good point. timeout rerun only if worker error indicates preemption (not global backlog). otherwise no auto rerun.

Sana Farid: i’ll write this up as a small “stats policy v0” snippet for the thresholds doc + send to @Jonas to implement in harness.

Jonas Weber: awesome. pls include reason codes we can pipe to UI:
- INCONCLUSIVE_MIN_N
- INCONCLUSIVE_EFFECTIVE_N
- INCONCLUSIVE_UNSTABLE_JUDGE
- INCONCLUSIVE_TIMEOUT
- FAIL_THRESHOLD

Selene Huang: and note that “UNSTABLE_JUDGE” should page the eval infra owner only if it’s widespread, not per-tenant.

Sahana Iyer: :thumbsup: i can add a dashboard panel for judge_error_rate + invalid_json rate.

Karthik Iyer: one more: if we allow only one infra rerun, we should store both attempts and show both in artifacts.

Olivia Grant: already planned: eval_run_ids[] in the gating summary.

Jonas Weber: cool. Sana can you drop draft in this thread tomorrow? we want to reference in the PRD update.

Sana Farid: will do. i’ll post a bullet list + some rationale (variance numbers) so it’s not “because vibes”.

Selene Huang: thanks. once we have it, i’ll sync with Aditya on UX wording for inconclusive vs fail.

Jonas Weber: closing the loop: current direction is NO borderline reruns for quality. reruns only for infra/judge instability. min N + effective N enforced. paired bootstrap CI for deltas. :thumbsup:
